headline_marked: Historic win: [[Bangladesh beat Australia in Test]] for the first time on their soil
headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test for the first time on their soil
summary: A nine-wicket victory in Darwin marks the country's biggest achievement in Test cricket, ending a 23-year wait for a win in Australia.
details: Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil and only their second win against the hosts.
The victory was achieved within four days, a feat hailed by former captain Akram Khan as the biggest achievement for Bangladesh cricket in the five-day game.
Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud provided a critical foundation, taking a career-best 6-55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on the opening day.
Tanzid Hasan scored his maiden Test century, supported by captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz to put Bangladesh in charge.
The result was particularly remarkable given that Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI days earlier.
BCB president Tamim Iqbal and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team, with Tamim describing the performance as 'extraordinary'.
Former selector Abdur Razzak noted that this win strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia in the World Test Championship.
caption:
A historic first! Bangladesh has just thrashed Australia in a Test match on their own soil for the first time ever.

Bangladesh secured a historic nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, marking their first-ever Test win on Australian soil and only their second win against the hosts.

The victory was achieved within four days, a feat hailed by former captain Akram Khan as the biggest achievement for Bangladesh cricket in the five-day game.

Fast bowler Hasan Mahmud provided a critical foundation, taking a career-best 6-55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on the opening day.

Tanzid Hasan scored his maiden Test century, supported by captain Najmul Hossain Shanto and all-rounder Mehidy Hasan Miraz to put Bangladesh in charge.

The result was particularly remarkable given that Bangladesh had been bowled out for just 54 in a warm-up match against a Cricket Australia XI days earlier.

BCB president Tamim Iqbal and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman congratulated the team, with Tamim describing the performance as 'extraordinary'.

Former selector Abdur Razzak noted that this win strengthens Bangladesh's case for more Test opportunities against Australia in the World Test Championship.

headline_marked: Iran's army chief warns [[he will 'break the legs' of Donald Trump]] over Hormuz Strait
headline: Iran's army chief warns he will 'break the legs' of Donald Trump over Hormuz Strait
summary: Major General Amir Hatami reacted sharply to Trump's claim that he would turn the strategically vital Hormuz Strait into US territory.
details: Iran's Army Chief Major General Amir Hatami has issued a stern warning to US President Donald Trump regarding the control of the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz.
Hatami stated that Iranian forces tasked with protecting the region would 'break the legs' of the US President if necessary, calling Trump's recent claims a 'dangerous joke'.
The warning comes after Trump suggested last Friday that he would turn the Strait of Hormuz into US territory, a move Iran views as a grave error.
Major General Hatami further claimed that US forces have been 'effectively expelled' from the region and no longer have permission to enter the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, or the Strait of Hormuz.
The Iranian military leader emphasized that US bases in the region will not be allowed to return to their previous status and that Iran will ensure this remains the case.

The Strait of Hormuz is a vital global energy artery, previously transporting nearly one-fifth of the world's total oil and LNG before Iran closed it following joint US-Israeli attacks on February 28.
Currently, shipping agencies report that only a few ships are able to navigate the strait, while the US maintains a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi also criticized Trump, calling him a 'criminal' and 'fool' and stating that the strait cannot be seized via tweets or aircraft carriers.
caption:
Iran's army chief warns he will 'break the legs' of Donald Trump. The tension over the Strait of Hormuz reaches a boiling point.

Iran's Army Chief Major General Amir Hatami has issued a stern warning to US President Donald Trump regarding the control of the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz.

Hatami stated that Iranian forces tasked with protecting the region would 'break the legs' of the US President if necessary, calling Trump's recent claims a 'dangerous joke'.

The warning comes after Trump suggested last Friday that he would turn the Strait of Hormuz into US territory, a move Iran views as a grave error.

Major General Hatami further claimed that US forces have been 'effectively expelled' from the region and no longer have permission to enter the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, or the Strait of Hormuz.

The Iranian military leader emphasized that US bases in the region will not be allowed to return to their previous status and that Iran will ensure this remains the case.

The Strait of Hormuz is a vital global energy artery, previously transporting nearly one-fifth of the world's total oil and LNG before Iran closed it following joint US-Israeli attacks on February 28.

Currently, shipping agencies report that only a few ships are able to navigate the strait, while the US maintains a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi also criticized Trump, calling him a 'criminal' and 'fool' and stating that the strait cannot be seized via tweets or aircraft carriers.
